note: Friend holds the batch delivery's turns (a note handed, deferred or given up after its bound) and the one-shot lanes (a card's turn needs the session unbroken but not the harness up, a harness fault keeps the card counted toward nothing, a card at its cap set aside after one turn), with the reversed witnesses deliverlimited, asideearly and faultcounts. A change of mode, the pacing's deferral of a batch turn, the lane sessions' opening, the reads, the step's drain of every ended result, the outbox's finishes off the loop and the refusal raise through tellBroken are below the module's grain. The spend cap (spendcap.go, a friend's per-day per-provider cap whose spend comes from the harness's usage report, that stops the turns and raises one judgment to the seat and the owner at the cap, or at once on a provider refusal for funds) is a new rule, outside the module.

FriendStage holds the daemon's staging of the jobs it writes: a stage begun only for a written brief, a lane handed a card only once its JOB.md is there, one judgment per unreachable repository or missing base while it stands, a stop that says nothing, and a failed job staged again once its remedy lands, with three reversed witnesses. The mirror's freshness window, the per-repository lock, the checkout's move-in, the step's drain of every ended result, the outbox's finishes off the loop and the refusal raise through tellBroken are below the module's grain; a read's checkout is not staged and is not in it.

Bus2 holds a send to every recipient and the log in one step (to and cc folded into one set), pending until ack, a live reader keeping its message while held under ClaimAfter, and a Stall that makes a holder idle past ClaimAfter claimable by any reader, with six reversed witnesses (partial, newfirst, steal, claimfresh, ackundelivered, ackreopens). bus.go cites those properties. A message's kind and RecvKinds, which releases a skipped kind at once, are not states in the module.
A member's presence on the fleet table, and the swarm's lease on a slot, have no module. A member's presence on the fleet table moved with internal/sprint to mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint in v1.2.3.

The merge queue, a card's promotion into it, and the member's tree have no module. Land models only the batch pushed from the queue. The two-level landing module CardISA cites is not in this tree. The merge queue and promotion moved with internal/sprint and cmd/nova-sprint to mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint in v1.2.3; the member's tree stays here.
No module, and no Go file in this tree, is an install that rolls back when ticks are missed. seat install (nova-sprint, now in mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint) is a different verb and is not this machine.

UpdateApply holds one run of the version inventory, the state file, and a delivery recorded per recipient scope only after the bus says SEND OK, with four reversed witnesses. A greater release version reads NEWER and AHEAD is the vX.Y.Z-0 pseudo-version only, as read.go reads them. The code delivers by nova-bus send. The older join path is gone; the module already names the bus only as that SEND OK.

CairnStore holds the session, the append, the log, the index and the coverage counts with no gap ledger, a re-open that names another publish policy refused, and a crash in Open healed by logging the open record, with three reversed witnesses (an overwrite, a report before fsync, a re-open with another policy). cairn.go writes an entry atomically, does not report before that write, implements no transport, and heals an interrupted open by logging the open record.

The table layer is the modelled layer (tla/README.md): contracts, member and epoch placement, edits, order, the shell, the function libraries, first contact and the fuse box. Each module has an expected-fail witness. TableMachine models the pinned baseline internal/tablemodel/testdata/table-pinned.lua, not today's pkg/nsprint/fn/lua/table.lua, and RedisFn names that witness without the word Broken in the configuration file; the plan's expected column is not pass.

CardContract holds the finish of a card, the member's push and the judgment, now split as the member runs it (member.go reportOne/reportRun, collectReports/applyReport): Judge names three finishes (ok, failed, reaped) with a refused push said first and a staging refusal, a provider failure with a reason, and a no-result end as reason prefixes on failed, so a provider end with no Provider and a no-result end are each modelled (the latter as a redeal class, never failed work, held by NoResultIsNotFailedWork); SendReport and CollectReport send the report and collect its result in two steps with Move enabled between them, a collected result applies only while the claim is held at the fresh queue read, else it is reaped (CollectedAppliesOnlyIfHeld), and an accepted report (code 0) is never reaped even when that acceptance moved the card to gen+1 (AcceptedIsNeverReaped); An assistant length cutoff, including an intermediate cutoff before a later stop or tool message, is a no-cost staging refusal before provider or synthetic-result fallback (LengthIsAHarnessFault); fourteen reversed witnesses. The sprint's side (a redeal, the retire at the redeal bound, a restage, the staging bound and the level) moved to nova-sprint in v1.2.3 and is outside the module. A finish or push file that is not a regular file is no record, the same absent record the module already finishes from, not a new state. keepUncertain's unknown-outcome keep-as-failed (no answer, changed=unknown) is below the module's grain. Push checks that the pushed origin head descends from the immutable stage record (RewriteKeptIsPushed); a direct update-ref below it is refused without changing origin or the stage record, and a repeated refusal is a stutter, with the rewritepushed reversed witness.

BenchRun holds one nova-ci bench run: the hosts in order, the make, copy, exec and remove steps on the first host that answers, and an interrupt that may land at any step, with an exec interrupt that kills the command (ranCmd, exit Killed) held by InterruptedExecRan, and two reversed witnesses (a failed copy that skips the deferred remove, an exec interrupt that refuses a run whose command ran). Every host's answer and every step's outcome is chosen by TLC, so the model covers each order of failure the code can meet.

BenchStage holds one bench's stage: the seed, the send measured from bytes, verification of the whole set before the first rename, a binary skipped when it already holds the release bytes, and a crash anywhere, with one reversed witness. The later stage-then-rename in install.go is that verify-before-rename.

ConfigApply holds a store write and its history row, the per-kind revision, Redis as a copy, the stamp after the ops, machine before friend, and the refusal rule (a refused write names its row and never stops the kind or a later kind, a kind with a refused op is not stamped, a row naming a row refused earlier in the run is refused with it when that row is absent from Redis or the ref field changes, a store error stops the run, CONFLICT and a kind check stop only their kind), with a sprint row (a ref to a friend) and a held live seat in its own instance (MCConfigApplySeat), no friend write refused for capacity (a friend row is width only; FriendWidthNeverRefused), and nine reversed witnesses (the old friend ceiling, a store error after a refusal swallowed, and the ref rule judged on the stored row with the seat held, among them). It was written from this code. Friend tiers and the bench registry set are outside the instance, which says field checks beyond the ref are.
A secret's placement, its sealing, and the seat's key have no module.
A decision's record, and the decision of one attempt, have no module.
FileLock holds the lock file's take and a stale holder, with four reversed witnesses. filelock.go cites the module. The only change since the module is the wording of the package comment.

Bus2Receipts (EXTENDS Bus2) holds the receipt states (delivered, read, acted) over the delivery machine, moved only by the Forward rule, and the daemon's recv (which stamps delivered, reads the receipt it found, and drops-and-acks a redelivered id), take, turn, ack, a lost ack and a crash, with ReceiptNeverMovesBack, ActedImpliesDelivered and NoIdActedTwice. A message given up is acked at read, and the present stamps the backlog delivered and acks it superseded. The failed acted stamp is owed, written again before the next read; three witnesses: a recv that hands every redelivered id (NoIdActedTwice), a recv that writes delivered over the receipt (ReceiptNeverMovesBack), and the known gap, a failed stamp, a lost ack and a crash together act a message twice (MCBus2ReceiptsKnownGap, Broken = losestamp). The step's drain of every ended result and the outbox's finishes off the loop (a-friend-step-collects-every-ended-lane-and-finishes-off-the-loop) are the loop's pacing, below this grain.

FriendEnvelope holds the full available pending set, the adapter text cap, the MaxBatch read cap while a present is owed, an exit-0 ack that is its own step and can fail, a failed message given up and acked once it reaches MaxDeliveries, accepted- and given-up-envelope acknowledgments, claim reopening and eventual delivery. EnvelopeTakesAll, NoYoungerFirst, AckOnlyAccepted and GivenUpOnlyAtTheBound hold with three reversed witnesses (newest-first, one-per-turn, give-up-early); the failure-reorder witness documents that a held failed message can be acknowledged after a younger one. The step's drain of every ended result and the outbox's finishes off the loop (a-friend-step-collects-every-ended-lane-and-finishes-off-the-loop) are the loop's pacing, below this grain. Metadata, authority labels and proof-id lifetime are below this model grain.

Caller-owned byte cursor over complete append-only records; bus return and process restart retain unread records; file replacement and truncation refuse. Broken EOF rearm skips an undelivered record. Prefix hash validation is the byte-level implementation fence, not an LLM receipt.

FriendLane holds a friend's lanes as thin clients of the sprint server, which keeps one record per (friend, lane, epoch): a lane asks what it holds (take --lane, its row and its lane and nothing else), runs exactly what the answer names, reports by the server's ids, epoch and lane, and drops the job on any refusal (save a LANE line it cannot read, on which it parks); a restarted lane asks first; a lane unheard past the bound is gone and its card bounces back; a clear is a new epoch. A work card runs with no begin (a read keeps its begin), and a row read that disagrees drops the card locally and the lane asks again. Invariants WorkingOnlyOnTheServersSay, OneRequestApart and NoStaleStep, liveness WorkingResolves and AllDone, with seven reversed witnesses (a took on an answer that named no card, a lane naming the epoch its directory says, progress at the directory's epoch that never leaves working, a lane that runs on after a refusal, a server that checks the card alone, a server with no gone bound, a lane that keeps running after a row read disagrees). The finish of a card held with a run's report before (TakenFinish) is modelled. The width (nova-tools#5726): the server holds it and changes it at any step (ChangeWidth), the client acts only on the copy its last read gave it (RowWidth: the daemon's row(), a member's Tick), and a lane starts a card only while its number is within that width and fewer lanes than it are live (a member's lanes by the count alone, Member); invariants LanesStartNeverPastWidth and NothingStartsUnanswered, action property NoLaneKilledOnLower, liveness WidthIsFilled, with four reversed witnesses (the lane-number gate alone, the floor of 1, a lower that cuts lanes, a width read only at the start). The parked lane (nova-tools#5724): an answer naming a card on a LANE line the lane cannot read (Garbled) is refused once and the lane parks, asking no more until its daemon restarts (Restart unparks; a clear or a width change does not), while the server's record of that card goes by the gone bound, fair for a parked lane as for a dead one; invariants ParkedRunsNothing, RefusedOnceNotALoop and ParkedNeverAsks, liveness ParkedRecordIsGone and ResumesAfterRestart, with four reversed witnesses (the ask again every TakeRetry before #5724, breaking RefusedOnceNotALoop, ParkedNeverAsks and, the asking lane never gone, WorkingResolves; a park that outlives the restart). Below the module's grain: the ask pacing, the brief and stage waits, the adoption of a working card no lane holds (a TakeGrant of a card the server already has working), her finish's next card, the clearing of a lane's hold by any other move (a Gone-like drop of the record), the read lanes' leases, Return as the stop-return (named by lane, as Owns), and Card.Epoch's directory-epoch fallback for a card the server named none for (the LocalEpoch witness's live behaviour).

FriendNotifications holds one receiver over the bus's pending entries with a durable ready bit: a deal notice is acked only once its ready notification is queue-accepted, its cards all taken (Withdraw, which clears the ready bit with nothing queued) or a newer notice replaces it (Coalesce), and a wake ping enters the urgent batch with the pong line (WakePing). NoLostReady, NoLostUrgent, ReadyQueueBounded and NativeUntouched hold with four reversed witnesses (withdraw-held, bad ack, bad duplicate, native mutation); FriendNotificationsCapacity names the Codex queue's read as the capacity, with BadQueue and BadHold failing QueueBounded and UrgentEligible. Below the grain: the adapter's delivered text, the batch byte cap and the report category's deferred journal.

Reach holds the ladder bus to push to window, starting partway up at From (the --from flag, StepsFrom the ladder's suffix): a proof stops it any time inside the bound (Prove), a push whose daemon is down or whose push fails is left at once before the bound (ClimbAtOnce), and a window without the accessibility permission refuses (Refuse, exit 2). NoStepAfterProof, EveryStepBounded and FailedOnlyAfterAllThree hold with two reversed witnesses (stepafterproof, fromtriedall). Below the grain: the nonce and pong text, the poll pacing and the bus log cursor.

LoopRedial holds the reader's connection to the sprint server: a restart drops the connection and the reader notices on the next verb's error, backs off one second doubling to MaxBackoff and re-dials on a fresh connection, so it never parks on a dropped connection (NoParkOnDropped) and beats again (BeatsAgain), with the wait bounded (BackoffBounded) and two reversed witnesses (noredial, nobound). The bytes of the wire, the asks themselves and the server's own state beyond the connections it holds are below the module's grain (sprintredial_test.go).

BusSendOnce holds a send under a token: the record written in the same step as the message (pkg/bus/redis.go AddOnce), a retry inside the life answered with the original and other arguments refused, and past the life refused with no second message, with four reversed witnesses (checkapart, newid, dropearly, nofingerprint). The model keys the record per token where the code keys it per sender and token, sound because the fingerprint includes From.

Delivery holds the present: a session start and a gap after Stale owe it, one turn carries the newest note from the seat (nothing while the seat is unknown), a one-shot present supersedes the note and delivers no turn, a present whose turn fails is owed again after a beat carrying the same note, fresh pings are answered and everything else superseded. GapCarriesThePresent, NoSupersededDelivered, NoStaleNonceAnswered and NoteFromSeat hold with four reversed witnesses (nopresent, reclaim, answerstale, anysender). The step's drain of every ended result and the outbox's finishes off the loop (a-friend-step-collects-every-ended-lane-and-finishes-off-the-loop) are the loop's pacing, below this grain. The acted receipt, the one-shot lanes and the bus-log status line are below this model grain.

a lane takes a card and holds it before it launches, and on STOP every running lane and every read is cancelled and owed a stop-return, a held card given up with its return owed, and every owed return sent whatever the word, with the heldthrough reversed witness; a batch turn already running goes on (a dealt-card turn started by startDealt, daemon.go), a v1.2.14 candidate

Hook holds the hook record of one identity and the role it is hooked as: a holder's start joins a record of its role and arms only where there is none (never over another role, never over an unhook, across a restart too), the identity's own word (nova-hook hook) arming over either, a holder renewing only under the epoch and role it joined, a lost record armed again by a running holder with its epoch counting from 0 again, a stopped holder's lease lapsing on its own, a daemon proving only a push it holds live, a challenge answered only by a session that read its nonce, and unhook moving the epoch on and clearing every lease and proof, with eight reversed witnesses. The window between a holder's death and its lease's expiry, the store's clock and a verb's own list of the roles it is for are below the module's grain.

HookBeat holds the v1.3 friend system: the hook's heartbeat (one pass an interval however many servers pass, a challenge left standing a whole interval a miss, a late answer refused, Limit misses in a row unhooking the name, logged once per hooking-in), only the live model answering, a silent model coming back and hooking in again; the tell of what the friends hear (the unhooked set and the coordinator) prepared by a pass, sent under a once-key whose write also marks the row's told, with failed sends, crashes and replays (NeverToldTwice; EveryTransitionToldAtLeastOnce under a fair sender); the judgments a tell raises (to the coordinator, COORDINATOR DOWN to every live name), open until answered and pushed OVERDUE once; the dashboard row as the table of the hook record (hooked, and answered within UpBound intervals of server time) and the hold, down for everyone when the server row is older than two intervals (StaleServerMeansDown; a silent friend shown down with every server stopped, under a fair clock alone); the client's own monotonic clock (its alarm only, never a record), asks expired once, the sprint's hold. Reversed witnesses: held while down, a daemon answering, unhook at three, two servers double-announcing, the dashboard reading a client's clock, told marked before the send (37e261311), told marked in a step after the send, up after an outage with no answer since, up with the server gone, no once-key. Partial: the code at 37e261311 marks told in the pass before the send, and the dashboard and the stale-row rule are modelled ahead of their code. Bootstrap models the client atomic skip while a challenge stands or beat_at owns the epoch, including after Answer; BootstrapPreservesServerNonce catches the old DEL/HSET overwriting the server nonce and removing until. BootstrapOnlyBeforeHeartbeat pins ownership until a new epoch. The bootstrap witness reaches a client challenge before the first heartbeat.

One bounded native call: owner discovery, single mutation attempt, accepted native evidence, external body isolation, inherited thread settings, and qualitative timeout. Linux measured all four declared outcomes on 2026-10-14; does not prove model ACK, filesystem security or concrete wall time.

Finite startup model: capture before publication, independent in-window per-ID answer filtering including out-of-order replies, current server challenge, one attempt per process and explicit duplicate startup recovery. Filesystem validation, concrete scan limits, 24h clock arithmetic and real model execution are below its grain. Linux measured all four declared outcomes on 2026-10-14.

One pending notice: a burst emits one line, notes that arrive while it is outstanding fold, and a turn boundary releases at most one more line. A busy publication writes the next generation and the busy word in one step, and that generation completes only when an idle snapshot of it is the sample, so a busy then idle pair between two reads still clears the notice. A failed write puts the count back. The bench configurations are owed; no cfg is in the tree until that run.
